title: Pan de elote
skill: A blender batter baked to doneness

move.title: Mastery: blend, bake, test
move.body: Pan de elote is a sweet Mexican corn cake, moist like a pudding in the middle. This is the unit's mastery week. You'll blend the batter while an adult watches but doesn't help, bake it, and decide for yourself when it's done with a toothpick.

callback.body: Your muffins were stirred just until mixed. In pan de elote, most of the batter is corn, eggs, and milk blended smooth; the flour goes in last and is pulsed only until it disappears.

why.title: The blender does the mixing
why.body: Blending the corn with the eggs and milk makes a smooth batter with little bits of corn. The flour goes in last for just a few pulses, so it doesn't get tough.

why.title: Condensed milk
why.body: Sweetened condensed milk is milk cooked down with sugar. It makes the cake sweet and very moist, so it needs only a little flour.

why.title: The toothpick test
why.body: This cake is moist, so the toothpick can come out with a few moist crumbs when it's done. Wet, runny batter means it needs longer.

wrong.sign: The middle is wet and runny
wrong.fix: Bake 5 more minutes and test again.
Lay foil loosely over the top for the last part of baking.
Turn it off and stir with the spatula, then blend again.
Let it cool longer. It sets as it cools.

quiz.q: Why does the flour go in last?
choices: So it's mixed only a little and stays tender

quiz.q: What makes pan de elote so moist?
quiz.explain: It needs only a little flour.

quiz.q: The toothpick has a few moist crumbs. Is it done?
quiz.explain: Wet, runny batter means not done.

ingredients.text: a little more, soft, for the dish

steps.text: Heat the oven to 350°F. Brush the baking dish with soft butter.
steps.look: The whole dish shiny with butter.

steps.text: Melt the 8 tablespoons of butter in the small bowl in the microwave.
steps.tip: Let it cool while you open the can.

steps.text: Crack the eggs into the blender.
steps.tip: Crack them on the counter so no shell falls in.

steps.text: Wash your hands with soap, and throw away the eggshells.
Add the corn, condensed milk, and melted butter. Put the lid on tight and blend.
steps.look: Smooth and pale yellow, with tiny bits of corn.

steps.text: Unplug the blender. Add the flour, baking powder, and salt. Pulse 4 or 5 times.
steps.tip: Don't taste the raw batter. It has raw egg.

steps.text: Pour the batter into the dish. Scrape out the blender with the spatula.
steps.look: An even layer in the dish.

steps.text: Bake until the top is golden and the middle is set.
steps.look: Golden on top, and the middle doesn’t jiggle.

steps.text: With oven mitts, pull out the rack. Push a toothpick into the center.

target.look: A clean toothpick, or a few moist crumbs, from the center

steps.tip: Wet batter? Bake 5 more minutes and test again.

steps.text: Turn off the oven. Let it cool in the dish, then cut it into 12 squares with the butter knife.
steps.tip: It sets as it cools, so wait before cutting.

eggs.text: Separate the eggs: crack each one and pass the yolk back and forth between the half shells over the medium bowl, letting the white drip into the bowl. Drop the yolks into the blender.
eggs.tip: Not a speck of yolk can get into the whites, or they won't whip. If a yolk breaks, save that egg for breakfast and use another.

flour.text: Unplug the blender. Add the flour and salt. Pulse 4 or 5 times.
flour.tip: Don't taste the raw batter. It has raw egg.

pour.text: Scrape the batter into the large bowl with the spatula.

add.text: Wash and dry the whisk. Whisk the egg whites in the medium bowl hard and fast until they're white, foamy, and hold soft peaks.
add.look: When you lift the whisk, the foam stands up in a peak that flops over at the tip.
add.tip: Take turns: it's hard work. An electric hand mixer is faster, if you have one.

add.text: Scoop the whites onto the batter in the large bowl. Fold them in gently with the spatula: cut down through the middle, sweep along the bottom, and turn the batter over the top. Turn the bowl and repeat until no white streaks are left.
add.look: A light, fluffy batter with no white streaks.
add.tip: Don't taste the raw batter. It has raw egg and raw flour.

add.text: Pour the batter into the dish and spread it gently into an even layer.
add.look: An even layer in the dish.

move.title: Mastery: blend, bake, test
move.body: Pan de elote is a sweet Mexican corn cake, moist like a pudding in the middle. This one is unleavened: whipped egg whites give it its lift. This is the unit's mastery week. You'll blend the batter while an adult watches but doesn't help, fold in the whites, bake it, and decide for yourself when it's done with a toothpick.

wrong.sign: The middle is wet and runny
wrong.fix: Bake 5 more minutes and test again.
Lay foil loosely over the top for the last part of baking.
Turn it off and stir with the spatula, then blend again.
Let it cool longer. It sets as it cools.
The whites weren't whipped long enough, or they were stirred in instead of folded. Next time, whip to soft peaks and fold gently.

quiz.q: Why does the flour go in last?
choices: So it's mixed only a little and stays tender

quiz.q: What makes pan de elote so moist?
quiz.explain: It needs only a little flour. The whipped whites lift it; they don't make it moist.

quiz.q: The toothpick has a few moist crumbs. Is it done?
quiz.explain: Wet, runny batter means not done.

add.title: Whipped whites lift it
add.body: Egg whites whisked hard trap thousands of tiny air bubbles. Folded gently into the batter, the bubbles swell in the hot oven and lift it a little. Stir hard and they pop, so fold, don't stir. It bakes a little denser than with a raising agent, and that's fine.
